"'''Ghostbusters'''" is a song written by American musician [[Ray Parker Jr.]] as the theme to the 1984 film ''[[Ghostbusters]]'', and included on [[Ghostbusters (1984 soundtrack)|its soundtrack]]. Debuting at number 68 on June 16, 1984, the song peaked at No. 1 on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] on August 11, staying there for three weeks (Parker's only number one on that chart), and at No. 2 on the [[UK singles chart]] on September 16, staying there for three weeks. The song reentered the UK Top 75 on November 2, 2008 at No. 49 and again on November 5, 2021, at No. 38.

The song was nominated at the [[57th Academy Awards]] for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] but lost to [[Stevie Wonder]]'s "[[I Just Called to Say I Love You]]". A lawsuit accusing Parker of basing the song's melody on [[Huey Lewis and the News]]'s song "[[I Want a New Drug]]" resulted in Lewis receiving a settlement.

"Ghostbusters" is a song written by American musician Ray Parker Jr. as the theme to the 1984 film Ghostbusters, and included on its soundtrack. Debuting at number 68 on June 16, 1984, the song peaked at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 on August 11, staying there for three weeks (Parker's only number one on that chart), and at No. 2 on the UK singles chart on September 16, staying there for three weeks. The song reentered the UK Top 75 on November 2, 2008 at No. 49 and again on November 5, 2021, at No. 38.

The song was nominated at the 57th Academy Awards for Best Original Song but lost to Stevie Wonder's "I Just Called to Say I Love You". A lawsuit accusing Parker of basing the song's melody on Huey Lewis and the News's song "I Want a New Drug" resulted in Lewis receiving a settlement.

For the soundtrack of the film's 1989 sequel, Ghostbusters II, Run-D.M.C. recorded a hip hop version of "Ghostbusters", featuring new lyrics. It was released on 7-inch vinyl and cassette as a standard single, as well as on 12-inch vinyl and CD as a double A-side maxi single with the track "Pause" from Run-D.M.C.'s fifth studio album, Back from Hell.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The song's music video begins with [[Sigourney Weaver]] and [[Annie Potts]] climbing out of a limousine in front of a large crowd, with Run-D.M.C., dressed in the standard beige Ghostbusters' uniform, accompanying them. The group then performs the song on stage to a packed audience for the remainder of the video, intercut with clips from the film. [[Bill Murray]], [[Dan Aykroyd]], and [[Ernie Hudson]] also cameo at the beginning of the video as security personnel.

British thrash metal band Xentrix covered the song and it was released as a single in 1990.  There was some controversy caused by the cover of the single, as the original artwork had an unauthorised use of the Ghostbusters logo (with the ghost giving the finger). The single was subsequently re-released using a different cover.

"'''Ghostbusters (I'm Not Afraid)'''", a version of the song by American [[Rock music|rock]] band [[Fall Out Boy]], featuring [[Hip hop music|hip hop]] recording artist [[Missy Elliott]], was released on June 23, 2016, from the [[Ghostbusters (2016 soundtrack)|soundtrack]] of the 2016 reboot ''[[Ghostbusters (2016 film)|Ghostbusters]]''. The cover received negative reviews from critics, who criticized its musical structure.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://consequence.net/2016/07/ray-parker-jr-responds-to-fall-out-boys-catastrophic-ghostbusters-theme-song/|title=Ray Parker Jr. responds to Fall Out Boy's catastrophic Ghostbusters theme song|work=Consequence of Sound|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=November 4, 2020|first=Collin|last=Brennan}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2016/06/ghostbusters-theme-fall-out-boy-cover|title=What Have We Done to Deserve Fall Out Boy's Ghostbusters Theme Song?|first=Hillary|last=Busis|magazine=Vanity Fair|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=November 4, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/music/la-et-ms-fallout-boy-missy-elliott-ghost-busters-theme-20160623-snap-story.html|title=Exactly how bad is Fall Out Boy's new 'Ghostbusters' theme song?|date=June 23, 2016|access-date=November 4, 2020|work=Los Angeles Times|first=Randall|last=Roberts}}</ref>

"Ghostbusters (I'm Not Afraid)", a version of the song by American rock band Fall Out Boy, featuring hip hop recording artist Missy Elliott, was released on June 23, 2016, from the soundtrack of the 2016 reboot Ghostbusters. The cover received negative reviews from critics, who criticized its musical structure.
